strongest_angle: Examine the 350th anniversary of King Philip's War, exploring the 14-month conflict in New England that stands as the bloodiest per capita war in colonial or US history.

key_facts.fact: King Philip's War, also known as Metacom's War, began in June 1675 in today's Warren, Rhode Island, and lasted for 14 months.
Metacom was an Indigenous leader from the Pokanoket people who led an alliance of New England tribes, including the Pokanoket, Nipmuc, and Narragansett.
The Indian Imprisonment Act was enacted in 1675 by the Massachusetts General Court in Boston and was not repealed until 2005.
The Great Falls Massacre occurred on May 19, 1676, at Peskeompskut on the Quinnehtukqut River in the Pocumtuck Homelands.
